newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek stocks climb to new highs in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Greek stocks climb to new highs in heavy volume.

text.p: Greek stocks ended 1.96 percent up on Tuesday on strong volume with analysts saying that more and more foreign and Greek investors were entering the Greek bourse and placing money in equities of all sectors.

"The 1,200 points that were overcome on Monday were a psychological resistance level. Market sentiment has been boosted and people keep investing in stocks," said Nikos Kostopoulos, an analyst at Commercial Securities.

January inflation, down to 6.8 percent year-on-year, from an expected 6.9-7.0 percent and the dropping interest rates helped the market to break the previous resistance level of 1,200 points on Monday.
"I expect the 1,270-1,300 level which is the new resistance level, to be tested this week," said Kostopoulos.

Other analysts said the investment public was shifting its interest from large- caps and rallying blue chips to smaller capitalisation stocks that were either left behind or had cheap prices and low P/E ratios.
Kostopoulos expected shares of National Bank to continue to lead the rally in the banking sector and investment and leasing shares to perform well.
Investment and leasing stocks are among the first to distribute dividends each year and because of this seasonality, they usually perform well in the first two to three months of the year, he said.
The Athens general share index finished 1.96 percent or 23.90 points higher at 1244.59 points from Monday's 1220.69, after opening at 1229.21.
Gainers led losers 167 to 68 with 25 issues unchanged on 260 traded. Turnover was 21.1 billion drachmas on volume of 7.0 million shares.
Banking shares rallied with a 3.25 rise followed by a climb in leasing shares of 1.92 percent. Investment gained 1.68 percent but insurance lost 0.65 percent. Construction shares firmed 0.20 percent.
Industrials ended 0.90 percent higher and small-caps closed up 0.11 percent.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted higher at 956.00-974.00. Shares of OTE telecom the underlying, ended 120 drachmas higher at 5,670.

The recently launched ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $27.87-$29.12. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The Morgan Stanley Hellenic Blue Chip Warrant, which has a strike price of 100 marks, was quoted higher at 9,613-10,196 drachmas.
